title: OpenAI-bridge v4: seed propagation and metadata forwarding for Responses
author: Anita Khatri
commits: a1b2c3: add initial bridge shim and request translation for responses v4
d4e5f6: propagate client_seed through compatibility layer and attach to response metadata
f7g8h9: streaming reassembly improvements to preserve seed-affine chunk boundaries
i1j2k3: forward user-provided metadata into internal ResponseRecord and telemetry
l4m5n6: SDK helpers and docs + e2e tests
o7p8q9: integration tests and CI matrix updates
description:
Context: Customers are starting to adopt the OpenAI Responses v4 style endpoint and expect parity with existing v3/v2 behavior for determinism controls and metadata propagation. Prior attempts preserved basic streaming compatibility but lost deterministic seed hints and user metadata when routed through the OpenAI compatibility layer. This caused flaky repros for customers relying on 'client_seed' and made audit logs incomplete.

This PR implements three coordinated changes to the compat bridge and runtime: 1) deterministic seed propagation: accept an optional client_seed|seed_hint field on the mapped Responses v4 request and reliably propagate it through the bridge into the internal InferenceRequest seed field (used by deterministic sampling kernels). Seed is stored on the canonical ResponseRecord so downstream logs/keys include it. 2) metadata forwarding: user-supplied metadata blob (freeform JSON) is attached to the ResponseRecord and surfaced in internal telemetry and audit exporters, with size-limits and sanitization. The compat shim no longer strips top-level user_metadata fields. 3) streaming stability + reassembly: streaming packets are now annotated with a stream_chunk_index and seed_affinity flag to ensure reassembly logic groups tokens emitted under the same seed context, preventing cross-chunk reseeding that caused non-deterministic outputs during stream reconnects. 

Checklist: 
- [x] API mapping and translation layer implementation (pkg/bridge)
- [x] Kernel/runtime plumbing to accept propagated seed (internal/runtime)
- [x] Streaming reassembly changes and tests
- [x] SDK helpers in python/ts to expose seed and metadata on client side
- [x] E2E tests and CI matrix updates
- [x] Docs (api-mapping/responses-v4.md)

Compatibility notes: This change preserves the existing default behavior when no seed/client_seed is provided. When a seed is supplied, it acts as a deterministic hint for sampling kernels; we do NOT guarantee bit-exact outputs across hardware variants. The seed is honored deterministically within a single runtime configuration. For customers using Dedicated or Private deployments, the seed propagation is a no-op unless the underlying runtime is configured to enable deterministic sampling.

Security and privacy: forwarded user_metadata is rate- and size-limited (4KB) and scrubbed of known sensitive keys (password, ssn, credit_card) with a best-effort redaction. Audit-exporter tests updated to include user_metadata.

Migration: No breaking changes to public Redwood API. OpenAI-compat clients can start attaching 'client_seed' and 'user_metadata' in Requests v4 body; SDK helpers added to python/ts to make this ergonomic.

Related: ENG-1347 (compat), ENG-1412 (streaming-reassembly), SUP-9021 (customer case).
review_thread: Diego Marquez: Please add one-line docs for behavior when seeds are absent. Added in docs, resolved.

Priya Nair: Will the seed_affinity mechanism increase latency for small requests? I couldn't find a perf regression on benchlab but please add notes. Reply: microbench shows <0.5ms median, included a note in CHANGELOG.
Tomoko Sato: Found a race in reassembly when client reconnects mid-chunk. Fixed with atomic chunk-id and added test.
release_notes: Add client_seed and user_metadata passthrough for OpenAI Responses v4 on the compatibility bridge; streaming reassembly updated to preserve seed affinity and improve reproducibility. SDK helpers and docs included.
